question: For all nonzero numbers \(x\) and \(y\) such that \(x=\frac{1}{y},\) \[ \left(x-\frac1x\right)\left(y+\frac1y\right) \] equals
solution:
The condition \(x=1/y\) means \(xy=1\). Since both numbers are nonzero, it also gives \(1/x=y\). Replacing the reciprocals reveals a difference-of-squares product:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left(x-\frac1x\right)\left(y+\frac1y\right)
&=(x-y)(y+x)\\
&=x^2-y^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the expression equals \(x^2-y^2\) for every allowed pair, choice D.
